I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (filled at $222.75, ≈$9,801 total), staying under the $10,000 per-order cap and within the $20,000 daily/ AAPL-MSFT-only buy mandate.

**Summary:** Apple's fiscal 2024 fourth quarter (ended Sept 28, 2024, reported Oct 31) showed reacceleration: quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full-year revenue of $391.0B. Full-year net income was $93.7B and diluted EPS $6.08 — both depressed by a one-time $10.2B income tax charge — while underlying profitability remained strong with operating income of $123.2B and operating cash flow of $118.3B, which I confirmed against the 10-K filed Nov 1, 2024. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand against the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so there was no negative catalyst to justify waiting. At $222.70 the stock trades at about 36.6x trailing EPS — not cheap, but reasonable for a cash-generative franchise with an AI-driven upgrade cycle ahead. I therefore took a partial, size-limited position (44 shares, ~$9.8K) at $222.75 — just above the ask, so close to market — rather than a full $10K allocation, keeping roughly $40K in cash and room for a second order today if a better entry appears.
